subject: SLO clarity: QPS, token-burst profile & next steps
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lowe <samantha@parcelflow.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: SLO clarity: QPS, token-burst profile & next steps

Hi Samantha — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick written recap so we can lock the numbers before we size a Dedicated estimate and surface any risks to infra. Please confirm/correct anything below.

High level footprint (from your session)
- Steady-state: ~40 QPS sustained (user-facing API) across 08:00–20:00 PST.
- Expected average payload: 220 tokens per request (this is the generated tokens; inputs average ~30 tokens).
- Peak events: marketing-triggered bursts. Two flavors: a short high-intensity spike (~600 QPS) that lasts ~5–7 minutes, and a broader campaign spike (~420 QPS) that can last ~15 minutes.
- Streaming mix: ~70% of requests use server-side streaming (progressive responses). Those streams are long-lived relative to standard requests — average stream duration 3.2s, avg output rate ~35 tokens/sec.
- Concurrency: concurrent active streams expected to be ~80 during steady-state, up to ~420 at peak if everything bursts concurrently.
- Tail latency targets: P95 generation latency goal of 250–300ms for non-streamed responses; for streamed responses P95 time-to-first-byte target 200–250ms and subsequent chunks sub-100ms.

What we need from ParcelFlow (next steps)
1) Confirm the peak numbers above and indicate whether peak 600 QPS is single-region only or multi-region.
2) Share the CSV you mentioned with per-hour QPS over the last 30 days (sample attached is fine).
3) Call out any hard SLOs (billing or user-facing) tied to these numbers — e.g., absolute P95 requirement or uptime SLA expectations.

What Redwood will deliver (next actions from our side)
- Quick back-of-envelope sizing for Dedicated GPU pools and a hosted fallback plan for the 600 QPS spike window.
- Workload-profile driven config suggestions: batching window, preferred model family (we'll propose a quantized variant if accuracy tests permit), and streaming buffer tuning.
- Draft mutual action plan and timeline for an evaluation run.

I've attached the sample workload CSV and the streaming trace you referenced (if anything else should be in that CSV, flag it). If these numbers look right I'll loop a capacity engineer for a short sizing note and marshal a short demo to show streaming tail behavior.

Proposed follow-up: 30-minute sync on Monday 2/16 at 10:00 PST to review sizing draft.

Thanks — Priyom

--
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference — inference that scales with predictability

Attachments: pf_workload_samples.csv, pf_streaming_trace_20260212.json
From: Samantha Lowe <samantha@parcelflow.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: ParcelFlow Engineering <eng@parcelflow.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 18:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLO clarity: QPS, token-burst profile & next steps

Priyom — thanks for the clear note, this aligns closely with what we said. Two small corrections and one addition:

- The 600 QPS spike is single-region (NA) and tied to a 5–7 minute ad-hoc campaign. We expect it ~3x per quarter, not daily.
- The 420 QPS peak is the expected traffic for predictable campaign windows and can last up to 15 minutes.
- Streaming mix is closer to 80% (not 70%) for the product flows that matter for latency-sensitive UX.

I attached a sanitized sample CSV (same naming you used) and a short stream trace — the trace shows a median RTT to first byte ~160ms but a noisy P95 closer to 320ms during a prior campaign (that was before a caching tweak).

Hard SLOs: our product team is targeting 99.8% availability for the text-generation endpoint and a user-facing P95 end-to-end <= 350ms for streaming-first-byte. We can accept occasional automated fallback to a lower-capacity model during extreme bursts, but need that to be flagged in the logs/alerts.

Confirming Monday 2/16 10:00 PST works.

Thanks,
Samantha
Director of Product — ParcelFlow
samantha@parcelflow.com

Attachments: pf_workload_samples.csv, pf_streaming_trace_20260212.json
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 08:11:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: SLO clarity: QPS, token-burst profile & next steps

Priyom / Rishi — forwarding Samantha's confirmation. Key updates for sizing:
- Increase streaming mix to 80%
- Expect single-region 600 QPS spikes 3x/quarter (5–7 min) and repeatable 420 QPS 15-min campaigns
- Target P95 streaming TTFB <= 350ms (customer target 350ms end-to-end)

Rishi — can you prioritize a quick Dedicated config sketch (GPU count, vCPU margin, Redis/kv cache sizing) and a hosted fallback runbook? Aim for an initial note by COB Monday so we have material for the 2/16 sync.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Feb 2026 09:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLO clarity: QPS, token-burst profile & next steps

Appreciate the clarifications, Samantha — that gives us what we need to draft a concrete plan. Action items and owners below (I'll upload the draft MAP to the Drive link and share ahead of the Monday sync):

Action items
- Rishi: initial Dedicated sizing sketch + cache sizing note (deliverable: one-pager; due: Mon 2/16 08:00 PST)
- Priyom: baseline streaming configuration (batching, token buffering) and proposal for graceful fallback policy (deliverable: doc + sample alert rules; due: Mon 2/16 09:00 PST)
- Marissa: pricing/contract guardrails we should present for a reserved commit covering expected steady-state + 2x headroom for peaks (deliverable: strawman pricing slides; due: Mon 2/16 09:30 PST)
- Samantha: confirm whether we want multi-region pre-warm for the 600 QPS spike or to rely on single-region autoscale + hosted fallback (deliverable: decision; due: Mon 2/16 09:00 PST)

Tentative Redwood baseline (ballpark, subject to review)
- Continuous Dedicated pool to cover steady-state: equivalent of 4x A10-class instances (GPU-backed) with autoscaling to handle gradual increases.
- Burst capacity: hosted-on-demand pool to cover up to an additional 300–400 QPS for short spikes; fallback routing rule will degrade to a quantized-small model if needed and surface alerts.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching recommended for repeated prompts — estimate Redis footprint ~20–30GB to capture hot prefixes for low-latency reuse.

I'll upload the Mutual Action Plan draft and the sizing sketch to the Drive link; thanks for the fast turnaround on the CSV/trace. See you Monday 2/16 10:00 PST.

Best —
Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
